title: Tiered kernel chooser and stability playbook for FlashAttn v2/v3
creator: Maya Chen
description: We continue to see non-deterministic latency spikes and occasional correctness regressions when mixing FlashAttention v2 and v3 variants across decode and prefill paths. This ticket captures an engineering plan to implement a 'tiered kernel chooser' that: 1) deterministically selects candidate kernels based on request fingerprint (seq_len, batch, precision, quantized flag, runtime shape histogram), 2) enforces guarded fallbacks during warmup, and 3) exposes a small set of knobs for canarying and rollback. The goal is to reduce jitter in P95/P99 latency and eliminate class of regressions caused by oscillating kernel selection during workload bursts.
success_criteria:
- P95 decode latency regression reduced to <= +5% vs baseline across canary workloads; P99 within +10%
- No new correctness regressions detected in replayed evals (prompt set) during a 48h canary
- Stable kernel selection entropy metric reduced by 60% for small-batch, long-context workloads
- Automated rollback trigger if error-rate or latency breach persists for 10 minutes
approach: 1) Implement deterministic scorer: map fingerprint -> ranked kernel candidates (v2/v3/quantized/compat) using offline cost model + occupancy heuristics. 2) Introduce 'warmup locks' that prefer conservative kernels for first N requests per endpoint/worker and then decay to cost-optimal choice. 3) Add a lightweight admission controller that can pin kernel choice for a session (function-call/streaming) to avoid oscillation. 4) Instrument kernel-choice telemetry and safety signals (latency delta, OOM signals, numerical anomalies). 5) Ship as opt-in flag with canary rollout and A/B analysis.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0: Unit tests + canary runtime build behind opt-in config (runtime branch runtime/attn-tiered-chooser)
- Stage 1: 1% of traffic on internal canary tenancy for 24h with aggressive telemetry
- Stage 2: 10% of traffic split across synthetic workloads + 2 customer sandbox tenants for 72h
- Stage 3: 50% with automatic rollback guardrails, escalate to on-call if thresholds tripped
- Stage 4: full rollout after 7d stable metrics
telemetry: We will emit kernel_choice_id, fingerprint_hash, preferred_rank, fallback_reason, latency_ms (per-token and per-request), memory_headroom_pct, oom_flag, numerical_error_flag, and selection_entropy(window=5m). Dashboards: /dashboards/runtime/attn-kernel-chooser; Alert: alert if P95 increases >10% or selection_entropy > baseline*0.4 for 15m.
experiments: Experiment A: cost-model-only chooser vs baseline (A/B) using internal prompt set, run 48h, collect token-level latency and QA accuracy
Experiment B: warmup-lock lengths (N=3,10,30) sensitivity test to find minimal conservative window
Experiment C: session pinning toggles (none, per-request, per-session) to measure decode jitter impact
Experiment D: compatibility mode enabling explicit v2-prefers for quantized models to test numerical stability
blockers: Need updated kernel-profile tables from Performance Team (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/perfbench/pull/112) and a resolve on the numeric anomaly detection API contract (spec in Confluence). Also waiting on infra quota to run 10% canary in dedicated cluster.
